reason: Conversation 1 reaches the correct diagnosis, a seized fan motor, from the customer's own checks (stiff, gritty blade, earlier grinding, hum). It also avoids naming a part number without the full model and tells the customer to find it from the full model number or use an engineer. It wrongly calls SA2 a 'model code' and is clumsy and thin in places, but SA2 is in fact the model series, so the error is minor. Conversation 2 gets SA2 right but wrongly calls the oven a double oven and fixates on the element. It then escalates a single, passing 'slight hot smell' into a stop-use, fire-risk alarm, never checks whether the fan spins or turns by hand, and never reaches the likely motor fault. That makes its advice poorly targeted and its escalation disproportionate.
